text:
ria: Quick heads-up: I opened a tiny PR to the OptKit migration doc that adds a compact Rust + Python example showing micro-batching + KV prefetch + an advisory on quant profiles. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4957
ash: love it. Rust snippets are rare in the guide — nice touch. can we make the Rust example use the async client pattern? folks using tokio expect that.
ria: done, switched to async and trimmed the snippet to 10 lines so it fits the sidebar.
noah: nit: the quant example currently presets `q4_0`. can we reword to recommend `q3_k` for seq<64 and call out tradeoffs (mem vs short-seq fidelity)?
ria: good call. changed wording to: "recommend q3_k for short-chat; q4_0 when memory is the primary constraint. monitor token-cost after switching."
ash: also add a one-liner CLI runnable example (`redwood-optkit run --profile q3_k --batch 6 --kv-prefetch`) so folks can smoke-test locally.
ria: added that line in a shell code fence. kept it single-line to avoid long-fence warnings.
ci-bot: preview-build: warning: missing-anchor `kv-prefetch` in docs/optkit/migrate.md — older versions might 404.
noah: link to canonical reference `/docs/sdk/reference/kv-prefetch` and add a parenthetical `(redirects from /legacy/kv)` to help bookmarks.
ria: updated the link and added the redirect note.
ci-bot: docs-lint: error: code-fence-language-missing in docs/optkit/migrate.md: updated samples need explicit fences.
ash: set fences to `rust` and `python` and add a caption line below: "Rust / Python equivalents."
ria: fixed. pushed.
docs-bot: deploy-preview: success — https://deploy-preview-4957--docs.redwood.ai
noah: quick wording tweak: change "use batching to save cost" -> "use micro-batching to reduce per-token cost while monitoring tail latency". less prescriptive.
ria: updated phrasing.
ash: LGTM.
noah: LGTM, approving.
docs-bot: CI: running full checks...
docs-bot: CI: green. all checks passed.
ria: merged. i'll file a small follow-up to add a more detailed Rust example in the cookbook later. thanks! :tada:
